title: ServiceAccount
description: A credential for CI that is not a person. It is named after the organisation, as <organisation>:<metadata.name>, has no email address and cannot sign in. It holds the member role unless spec.role says developer or owner. A member cannot invite people, mint further credentials or change policy. A developer service account can plan, apply and export every kind, ServiceAccount included, and so is the credential to give Terraform or CI that applies Platform IaC. An owner service account can do everything an owner can. Applying a new ServiceAccount creates it and returns its API key and secret once, in the apply result's status (status.apiKey and status.secret): they are never shown again, by plan, export or the console, so store them as the apply returns them. Applying needs an owner, an admin or a developer. Only an owner can declare an owner; a developer declares member or developer service accounts and cannot change or delete an owner one. Deleting the document deactivates the service account, so its key stops working; it is kept for the audit trail, and its name cannot be used again.

metadata.description: The name is 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, such as ci-scanner.

spec.description: A service account declares its name and, optionally, its role.

role.description: member, developer or owner. member (the default) can scan and read but cannot change policy. developer can apply Platform IaC for every kind, service accounts up to developer included, but in the console cannot manage members, invitations, billing, the vault, service accounts or Drift protection: it is the credential to give Terraform or CI. owner can do everything an owner can. Only an owner may declare owner; an owner or a developer may declare developer. admin is a retired role that a person can no longer be given and a service account cannot hold: the schema still accepts the word so that documents written for v1.16.0 validate, and applying one is refused.
